newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya will host summit on conflict in east Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Kenya will host summit on conflict in east Zaire.

text.p: A summit of at least seven African states in Kenya on November 5 will focus on the war in eastern Zaire, a Kenyan official said on Friday.
David Kikaya of the foreign ministry said Kenya had invited Zaire to attend but had received no official response yet.
Zaire on Thursday said it would not be involved in any talks until Rwandan troops had left its territory. Rwanda denies it has forces inside Zaire backing ethnic Tutsi rebels.
"We are going ahead with our plans for the summit and hope Zaire will change its mind and come," Kikaya, of the ministry's press division, told Reuters.
"The summit is basically about the Zaire situation. Developments in eastern Zaire are complicating the efforts of regional heads of state to resolve the crisis in Burundi," he added.
Kenya said on Thursday night President Daniel arap Moi would meet the leaders of Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Rwanda, Ethiopia and Cameroon in Nairobi next Tuesday.
The U.N. and European Union are pressing for the rapid convening of a regional conference to discuss the humanitarian and political crisis in the Great Lakes area of central Africa.
They say a ceasefire in eastern Zaire must be quickly agreed.
But Zaire, whose ragged army has suffered reverses against Tutsi rebels, sounds in no mood for a ceasefire or talks.

"The government will not undertake any negotiation, will not participate in any regional conference while a part of national territory is occupied by foreign forces," Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo told an emergency parliament session on Thursday.

"This war which the combined forces of Uganda, Burundi and Rwanda are waging against Zaire has brought to broad daylight Rwanda's intention not to welcome on its territory its nationals living in Zaire and to pursue its insane plan of annexing a part of our territory," he said.
The group invited to Nairobi has met several times in the past months to agree policy on Burundi and imposed sanctions on that country on July 31 as a penalty for a military coup.
Zaire has previously taken part in the Burundi summits.
